summary: ACCEPT. Schedules the D6 fan-out outcome acceptance report. REBASE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, not accepted on report: I computed git patch-id --stable on both sides myself and got d8034a0e5e175f2e5c901f27a3e32416a9b67996 for the old range (f2296c24..5fac14d1) and the identical d8034a0e for the new range (bb5d3964..086b4d3c), and confirmed bb5d3964 is an ancestor of the new head. The rebase carried no content change. THE BLOCKING ITEM IS CLOSED BY EXECUTION: B1, the mid-install rollback gap, was proven at three widely separated injection points - in every one the on-disk artifact SHA stayed in sync with the crontab-armed SHA. The mechanism is a single EXIT trap (INS:142) plus a transaction flag raised after backups and before the first install (INS:184) and lowered on the last line (INS:296), unwinding in reverse: crontab from its pre-image verified with cmp -s, then check.py, then cron.py. THREE MUTANTS ARE COVERED BY INSPECTION, NOT BY AN EXECUTED MUTATION RUN. The run was killed for wall-clock time at the operator's instruction after a prior harness had a restore bug that contaminated its own baseline; I verified the tests by reading the tree instead. M1, whole-line schedule matching (grep -Fxc -> -Fc): killed by a four-way controlled set on one variable at test file lines 879/882/885/889 - absent, present, duplicated, and critically COMMENTED (hash-space-line), which -Fc accepts and -Fxc rejects, with the positive control adjacent. M2, runtime import replaced by compile(): killed by a parametrized pair at lines 1651-1652 supplying a module-scope raise RuntimeError AND an import of definitely_missing_d6_dependency producing ModuleNotFoundError - compile() catches neither, so unlike the earlier SyntaxError-only case from round 10 the kill is not incidental. M3, moving the preservation check after the crontab write: killed by test_lossy_successful_awk_is_refused_before_root_crontab_is_written at line 1531, which names the ordering property directly, alongside two sibling tests at 928 and 1490. NOT MEASURED, stated so it cannot decay into a pass: no mutant was executed against a baseline for M1/M2/M3, so what is established is that a named test exists whose asserted input distinguishes the mutated behaviour - not an observed red. A test that is present and well-aimed can still be vacuous in a way only execution reveals; that residue is real and is accepted deliberately here on scope grounds, not overlooked. SCOPE JUSTIFYING THAT ACCEPTANCE: this PR is ops-only. It restarts no service, is invoked by hand, and its blocking harm - the rollback gap - is the item that IS executed-proven. The three remaining mutants guard already-correct behaviour against regression rather than fixing a live defect.
